subject: Best practices for drawing path diagrams?

messages.author: 32db9d7f15ef6f0b
messages.subject: Best practices for drawing path diagrams?
parts:
Dear fellow lavaan users,

I was wondering how you go about drawing path diagrams based on the parameter estimates that lavaan delivers. Is there a better option than drawing it by hand, e.g., by involving tikz somehow? Any advice would be greatly appreciated.

Thank you,
Bertolt

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Best practices for drawing path diagrams?
parts:
On 09/13/2012 03:30 PM, Bertolt Meyer wrote:
> Dear fellow lavaan users,
>
> I was wondering how you go about drawing path diagrams based on the
> parameter estimates that lavaan delivers. Is there a better option than
> drawing it by hand, e.g., by involving tikz somehow? Any advice would be

The qgraph package produces some nice diagrams (using a network
approach). And it understands lavaan objects.

For publication, I use Latex+Tikz. Manually.

Yves.

Bertolt

An automatic way to draw CFA's from lavaan with R comes with the
psych-package by Revelle.
The following is from his lesson 'Psychology 454: Latent Variable
Modeling', see slide 28 from
http://personality-project.org/revelle/syllabi/454/wk6.lavaan.pdf.

library(psych)
library(lavaan)
b2 <- Bechtoldt.2[c(3:8,15:17),c(3:8,15:17)]
Thurstone.mod <- ' F1 =~ Sentences + Vocabulary + Completion
F2 =~ First_Letters + Four_letter_words + Suffixes
F3 =~ Letter_Series + Pedigrees + Letter_Grouping'

t.cfa.2 <- cfa(Thurstone.mod,sample.cov=b2,sample.nobs=213,std.lv=TRUE)
summary(t.cfa.2)


lavaan.diagram <-
function(fit,model="cfa",...) {
if(model=="cfa") {
fx=fit@Model@GLIST$lambda
colnames(fx) <- fit@Model@dimNames$lambda[[2]]
Phi <- fit@Model@GLIST$psi
Rx <- fit@Model@GLIST$theta
v.labels <- fit@Model@dimNames$lambda[[1]]

structure.diagram(fx=fx,Phi=Phi,Rx=Rx,labels=v.labels,...)
} else
{structure.diagram(fx=fit@Model@GLIST$lambda,Phi=fit@Model@GLIST$beta,
Rx=fit@Model@GLIST$theta,...) }
}
lavaan.diagram(t.cfa.2)

Alternativly if one wishes to plot with R, one needs to call RGraphviz
or qplot and build up all from the skretch.

regards,
Ren�

parts:
If you are using LaTeX already, you might consider tikz for your path diagrams, e.g., 

\documentclass[border=3mm]{standalone}
\usepackage{tikz}
\usetikzlibrary{arrows,positioning}
egin{document}
egin{tikzpicture}[auto,node distance=.5cm,
latent/.style={circle,draw,very thick,inner sep=0pt,minimum size=30mm,align=center},
manifest/.style={rectangle,draw,very thick,inner sep=0pt,minimum width=45mm,minimum height=10mm},
paths/.style={->, ultra thick, >=stealth'},
]

ode [manifest] (SI) at (0,0) {Similarities};
ode [manifest] (VO) [below=of SI]  {Vocabulary};
ode [manifest] (CO) [below=of VO]  {Comprehension};
ode [manifest] (IN) [below=of CO]  {Information};
ode [manifest] (WR) [below=of IN]  {Word Reasoning};
ode [manifest] (BD) [below=of WR]  {Block Design};
ode [manifest] (PS) [below=of BD]  {Picture Concepts};
ode [manifest] (MR) [below=of PS]  {Matrix Reasoning};
ode [manifest] (PC) [below=of MR]  {Picture Completion};
ode [manifest] (DS) [below=of PC]  {Digit Span};
ode [manifest] (LN) [below=of DS]  {Letter-Number};
ode [manifest] (AR) [below=of LN]  {Arithmetic};
ode [manifest] (CD) [below=of AR]  {Coding};
ode [manifest] (SS) [below=of CD]  {Symbol Search};
ode [manifest] (CA) [below=of SS]  {Cancellation};

ode [latent] (g)  [left=2.5cm of MR]  {\emph{g}};
ode [latent] (Gc) [right=4.5cm of CO] {Verbal\ Comprehension};
ode [latent] (Gv) [right=4.5cm of BD] {Visual\ Spatial};
ode [latent] (Gf) [right=4.5cm of PC] {Fluid\ Reasoning};
ode [latent] (Gsm) [right=4.5cm of LN] {Working\ Memory};
ode [latent] (Gs) [right=4.5cm of SS] {Processing\ Speed};

oreach \all in {SI, VO, CO, IN, WR, BD, PS, MR, PC, DS, LN, AR, CD, SS, CA}
{
\draw [paths] (g.east) to node  { }   (\all.west);
}

oreach \vc in {SI, VO, CO, IN, WR, PC}
\draw [paths] (Gc.west) to node  {}   (\vc.east);

oreach \vs in {BD, MR, PC, SS}
\draw [paths] (Gv.west) to node  {}   (\vs.east);

oreach r in {PS, MR, AR}
\draw [paths] (Gf.west) to node  {}   ( r.east);

oreach \wm in {DS, LN}
\draw [paths] (Gsm.west) to node   { }   (\wm.east);

oreach \ps in {CD, SS, CA}
\draw [paths] (Gs.west) to node  {}   (\ps.east);

\end{tikzpicture}
\end{document}


Best,

Alex
